rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With he / she / it the verb takes -s, even in the negative: 'He doesn't like it'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: With I / we / you / they the verb has no -s: 'They don't like it'.

rules.label: Subject-verb agreement
rules.why: 'I am' in the present, 'I was' in the past. Never 'I is'.

rules.label: Present perfect needs a participle
rules.why: After have / has / been the verb must be the past participle: 'I have gone', not 'I have went'.

rules.label: Past tense needs the base verb
rules.why: After don't / doesn't / didn't the verb goes back to its base form: 'I didn't go', not 'I didn't went'.

rules.label: Double comparison
rules.why: Do not use 'more' with a word that is already comparative: 'more better' becomes 'better'.

rules.label: Double superlative
rules.why: 'Most' doubles the superlative: 'most best' becomes 'the best'.

rules.label: Modal verb never takes to
rules.why: Modal verbs stand alone: 'can go', 'must go' - never 'can to go'.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: 'Agree' is a verb. Say 'I agree' or 'I am in agreement with you'.

rules.label: Extra preposition
rules.why: 'Discuss' is transitive and takes no 'about': 'discuss the plan'.

rules.label: Explain needs to me
rules.why: 'Explain' takes the thing first, then the person: 'explain it to me'.

rules.label: Uncountable noun
rules.why: 'Advice' has no plural. Say 'a piece of advice'.

rules.label: Uncountable noun
rules.why: This noun has no plural in English: 'information', 'advice', 'equipment'.

rules.label: Wrong idiom
rules.why: The phrase is 'regardless of' or 'in spite of'.

rules.label: Wrong idiom
rules.why: 'Despite' takes no 'of': 'despite the rain'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: For a duration use 'for': 'for three years'. Use 'since' with a point in time: 'since 2020'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: The set phrase is 'interested in something'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: Always 'depend on' - never 'depend of'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: 'Marry' takes no preposition: 'I married Ali'.

rules.label: Wrong preposition
rules.why: After 'wait' use 'to' + base verb: 'waiting to see'.

rules.label: Correct preposition
rules.why: Good - keep 'depend on' and 'concentrate on'.

rules.label: Repetition
rules.why: One 'same' is enough.

rules.label: Doubled word
rules.why: The word is repeated - a slip of the keyboard or the tongue.

rules.label: Redundant
rules.why: 'Age' is not needed after 'years old'.

rules.label: Fixed expression
rules.why: The set phrase is 'in conclusion', no article.

rules.label: Redundant
rules.why: 'By the time' already means 'when'.

rules.label: Double determiner
rules.why: Choose one: 'every student' or 'each student'.

rules.label: Over-specified
rules.why: 'Both' already means two: 'both students'.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: The verb is 'affect', the noun is 'effect': 'the effect of the rain'.

rules.label: Missing apostrophe
rules.why: 'You're welcome' and 'you're right' use the contraction 'you are'.

rules.label: Possessive vs contraction
rules.why: 'Its' shows possession; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

rules.label: Double comparison
rules.why: Use one comparative only: 'more than', not 'more than more'.

rules.label: Missing auxiliary
rules.why: The negative needs a helper verb: 'I don't understand', never 'I no understand'.

rules.label: Wrong word order
rules.why: With I / we / they the progressive is am / are + V-ing: 'I am learning'.

rules.label: Third person singular -s
rules.why: With he / she / it the present simple verb takes -s: 'He goes to school'.

rules.label: Wrong word
rules.why: 'Agree' is a verb: 'I agree with you', not 'I am agree'.

rules.label: Duration phrase
rules.why: 'for' goes before the duration: 'for three years'.
